To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a genomic island, Pgi-1, has been identified in the genome of R. solanacearuma biovar 2 strain KZR- 5.
a 17.5-kb genomic island (PGI-1) has been deleted in an environmental Ralstonia strain (KZR-5).

we found a deletion in the genome of the novel environmental Ralstonia strain KZR- 5 as compared to the potato reference strain 715 and that the deleted region, PGI- 1, is homologous to a region in the genome of potato strain 1608.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genomic plasticity of a plant pathogen in response to environmental selection pressure.
the identification of a genomic island in R. solanacearun biovar 2 that may have been acquired during adaptation of the bacterium to the aquatic environment.
a novel genomic island, Pgi-1, which is deleted in the genome of an environmental strain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PGI-1 is not required for the virulence on potato, but is involved in the adaptation to the environment.
the PGI-1 deletion has no effect on the ecological behavior of strain 715.
the deletion of PGI- 1 in strain KZR- 5 is a neutral event, but that the deletion of the IS elements at either end of the island might be of importance in the life history of strain KZR5.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of Pgi-1 in the environmental strain KZR5 has no apparent effect on virulence or temperature tolerance.
PGI-1 may have been lost during the adaptation of strain KZR 5 to the aquatic environment, which may explain the enhanced cold tolerance of this strain.
the loss of a putative genomic element PGI-1 is associated with an adaptation to cold temperatures, which is a prerequisite for survival in temperate climate zones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genome of biovar 2 is more diverse than anticipated, and that the genome of strain KZR5 is a good candidate for a biocontrol agent against potato brown rot.
the genomes of biovar 2 isolates are not clonal, and that a PGI-1 island is lost from the environmental strain.
, despite its clonal genome, R. solanacearun biovar 2 is a highly dynamic species.
